clue.text: Doesn't compete, yet scores

definitions.meaning: a horse or player that pulls out of an event before it starts withdraws in this sense
to score is to mark a surface with lines or gouges

explanation.surface: An athlete who stays out of the race still somehow piles up points.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing from a contest and making marks on a surface are both meanings of the same verb.

clue.text: To cheat over money is mean

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them
a note is a piece of paper money

explanation.surface: A moral pronouncement that swindling someone out of cash is a mean act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective (stingy), but it is the verb: to signify.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply or suggest a further meaning is a verb sense of mean, as words carry overtones.

clue.text: A ring formed with gunmen in charge

indicators.note: the gunmen are placed in among the rearranged letters
the letters of a ring are formed into a new shape, an anagram signal

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men in command form a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges A RING into ARIGN, and 'in' puts RA (Royal Artillery) inside it after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone in court of a crime is to bring a charge against them.

clue.text: Business left to slip into chaos

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: A company left to itself falls into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the noun: a collapse is a state of breakdown and chaos; 'to' and 'into' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A total breakdown or failure of order is a collapse, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Get rescue organised

indicators.note: the letters of rescue are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange a rescue mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or acquire something is a common sense of both words, as in securing a deal.

clue.text: One excuses the traveller running water without point

parts.note: a rep, a commercial traveller, is a salesman on the road

indicators.note: here without means outside, so the river surrounds the point

parts.note: a river is a stretch of running water
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone forgives the traveller for making water pointlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside': RIVER goes round E to make RIEVER, not 'lacking' a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grants a stay or pardon from punishment lets the offender off, so one who excuses.

clue.text: Taste was the guide involved

parts.note: a tang is a sharp distinctive taste
one who was the guide led the way

explanation.surface: A guide who tasted things was implicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved is complicated and knotted, as a convoluted plot is said to be.

clue.text: Having unfinished sculpture to transport as ordered

indicators.note: the sculpture is left unfinished by losing its last letter

parts.note: a statue is a piece of sculpture
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A half-made sculpture is to be shipped according to instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required by law is laid down by statute, so done as ordered.

clue.text: Smart English worker taking in trainee for example

indicators.note: the English worker absorbs the next pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's standard worker
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A sharp-dressed English employee takes on a learner as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and well-dressed in a refined, graceful way, as a stylish outfit might be called.

clue.text: Any girl making up in a mad way

indicators.note: the letters of any girl are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A girl putting on make-up in a furious temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of furious, so acting in a mad way is acting crossly.

clue.text: Support raised by Tories

parts.note: up means raised, as a hand that is up
the Right is the political wing of the Conservatives or Tories

explanation.surface: Funding put up by the Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical post holding something up is a structural support in a building.

clue.text: He's moved one large container into the car

indicators.note: the container goes into the car, inside its letters

parts.note: a motor is a car
I is the Roman numeral for one
a vat is a large tank or tub

explanation.surface: Someone shifting house loads a big tank into the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's moved' reads as someone who has relocated; it means one who moves others to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inspires others into action stirs them, so people are moved by such a person.

clue.text: The Moor rings about the double figure

indicators.note: the rings are placed about the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: rings are two round letters O
taken as written

indicators.note: the figure that follows is written down twice, side by side

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral, a figure, for fifty

explanation.surface: A Moorish figure wears rings around a two-faced idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double figure' is L, the Roman numeral fifty, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Moor of Venice, so the title character is known as the Moor.

clue.text: Housing for the fellows engaged in teaching

indicators.note: the fellows are engaged in, or held inside, the teaching

parts.note: a tenet is a doctrine or teaching
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Accommodation for male staff who work as teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, a form of urban housing.

clue.text: Turning evil, trap game

indicators.note: both pieces together are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: sin is evil
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A gangster turned bad sets a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played over a net is a well-known game.

clue.text: Court officials hired help top divide gratuities

indicators.note: the hired help splits the gratuities by going between their letters

parts.note: tips are gratuities
staff are hired help

explanation.surface: Court officials take on paid helpers to share out the tips.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'top' is an OCR misreading of 'to'; 'divide' means the hired help splits the gratuities by sitting inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers carrying a metal-tipped staff of office who serve in law courts, an old legal title.

clue.text: It's rough for the partisan

definitions.meaning: uneven, not smooth or regular in shape
a guerrilla fighter outside a regular army

explanation.surface: Life is hard for a resistance fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven or bumpy covers one sense; a soldier not in the regular army, like a guerrilla, covers the other.

clue.text: Repeatedly let loose

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to lease is to let property

explanation.surface: Someone is set free again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is the verb, to set free; RE- plus LEASE reads as let again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set loose or free a captive is the verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Dolts can go to pot in this country

indicators.note: letters that go to pot fall into disorder and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Idiots may ruin themselves in this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of the United Kingdom, north of England, is a country.

clue.text: Shrinking from giving drink to about a hundred

indicators.note: the drink-giving goes about the hundred, enclosing it

parts.note: wining someone, as in wining and dining, is giving them drink
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from serving alcohol to a crowd of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Flinching or recoiling in pain is shrinking back.

clue.text: Ill-natured lament about able seaman, second class

indicators.note: the lament goes about the sailor and class, enclosing them

parts.note: to cry is to lament
AB is the abbreviation for able seaman
B is the second class or grade

explanation.surface: A grumpy sailor rated second-class complains.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouchy and bad-tempered, as cross as a crustacean is said to be.

clue.text: Simple but by no means specific

definitions.meaning: a simple is a medicinal herb
a specific is a remedy for one disease; this plant claims to cure everything

explanation.surface: Something plain but vague.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant valerian, a herbal remedy reputed to cure all ills, is the opposite of a remedy for one complaint.

clue.text: Keep scholars in to put straight

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates or scholars

indicators.note: letters put straight are sorted out into a new order

explanation.surface: Students kept in after school to be set right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put straight' sorts IN TO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a fortified stronghold, and a bastion is a projecting fortification.

clue.text: Vindictive, but possibly lets up if required

indicators.note: the letters of lets up if could possibly be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A vengeful person who might ease off if asked to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if required' adds to the surface; 'possibly' rearranges LETS UP IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malice, so someone full of it seeks revenge.

clue.text: Speaks of unqualified school-head

parts.note: utter means complete or unqualified, as in utter nonsense
the head of school is its first letter, S

explanation.surface: Talks about an unqualified headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying words aloud is speaking them.

clue.text: Totally lacking bite

parts.note: literally a mouth with nothing to bite with; figuratively a law or threat with no force

explanation.definitionFit: Without any power to bite, literally from having no teeth, or figuratively ineffective.

clue.text: Bill is a relation

definitions.meaning: a bill is a statement of charges
a relation is a narrative or report

explanation.surface: A bill is a kind of relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of money owed and a report or narrative of events are both senses.

clue.text: Arbiter taking a break for a quick meal

indicators.note: the arbiter's letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee takes a pause for a fast snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a quick British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Melted cheese on toast is a light, quickly made meal or snack.

clue.text: Note: not just a place of entertainment

parts.note: F is a musical note
unfair means not just

explanation.surface: A memo complains that a venue is unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling show with rides and stalls is a place of amusement.

clue.text: Wrapping up well, put on pounds-—move around!

indicators.note: the moving goes around the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to swing is to move to and fro
to add weight is to put it on
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone bundled up warmly gains weight and has to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding a baby tightly in cloths is wrapping it snugly.
